title: Exam review: Module 2 · skin lesions, tumours & skin surgery
summary: All 30 questions from the Module 2 end-of-module exam, with the recommended UK answer, why the distractors are wrong and links to the matching condition pages. Themes: Vascular vs malignant lookalikes, adnexal tumours, AK vs Bowen’s, anatomy and electrosurgery.

article.title: About this review
blocks: Revision key for the DermUSW end-of-module exam for Module 2 (Dec 2023): 30 single-best-answer questions. **Saved** is the answer ticked before submission (not a graded course key). **Recommended** is the teaching answer on current UK guidance (NICE / CKS, BNF, BAD, BASHH, Resuscitation Council UK, UKHSA).

rows: Young woman, rapidly growing bleeding papule after a scratch; granulation-like capillaries with epithelial collarette

Rapid growth after trauma, friable, collarette on histology. Amelanotic melanoma is the important DDx, so **always send for histology**. Bacillary angiomatosis needs HIV/Bartonella. Glomus is painful and subungual. KS is spindle cells and HHV-8
Warty papules on the backs of hands/feet since childhood, "church-spire" hyperkeratosis, palmar pits

Linked to Darier disease (ATP2A2), which explains the palmar pits. EDV is HPV-driven flat warts with malignant potential. Stucco keratoses appear in older people. AK is sun-damaged older skin. Viral warts have no palmar pits and are not lifelong
58-year-old farmer, nodular flesh-coloured neck lesion with telangiectatic rolled edge; next step to *establish the diagnosis*

Looks like nodular BCC. UK practice: diagnostic **excision with a 4 mm margin** for a well-defined primary BCC (BAD BCC guideline, NICE CSG8) gives diagnosis and cure together. If unsure, a **punch/incisional** biopsy is used. **Shave biopsy** misses depth/subtype for nodular lesions. Tru-cut is for deep masses, triamcinolone is for keloid, and microneedling is cosmetic

BCC is slow-growing and rarely metastasises, so elective surgery can wait. Local anaesthetic is safe if surgery is needed, but there is no urgency. Cryotherapy is unsuitable for nodular BCC. Radiotherapy in pregnancy is inappropriate
60-year-old man, "moles of concern" on his back (image)

New or flat junctional naevi are unusual at 60, because naevi mature to compound or intradermal with age. Irregular, multiple lesions in an older adult fit atypical naevi. Use the image: if one lesion meets the ABCDE/7-point checklist, think melanoma and **refer on the suspected-cancer pathway (NICE NG12)**
Bluish-black plaque since childhood, new satellite, blue-white veil, atypia, S100/Melan-A positive
A melanoma arising in or resembling a blue naevus: change, a satellite and atypia. LMM is facial and chronic sun damage. Pigmented BCC is S100-negative. KS is a vascular tumour
[Halo naevus](condition:halo-naevus), [blue naevus](condition:blue-naevus), [Spitz and Reed naevi](condition:spitz-naevus), [Melanoma: recognition & referral](condition:melanoma)
Nodular melanoma: Breslow 4 mm, ulcerated, mitoses 1/mm²; strongest predictor of survival
AJCC 8 T-stage is based on Breslow + ulceration, and Breslow is the strongest single predictor. Clark level is no longer used for staging. Mitotic rate was dropped from AJCC 8 T1 staging
Pacemaker (recent battery, regular review), BCC on abdomen >5 cm away; electrosurgery
**Bipolar** short bursts + monitoring + arrest trolley + **inform cardiac physiology**. Option 4 is the likely course key; option 1 (bipolar + pre/post checks) is acceptable and more cautious

Bipolar current stays between the forceps tips, so pacemaker interference is minimal. Monopolar current runs through the patient and can cause oversensing or inhibition. With a stable, recently checked **pacemaker** (not an ICD), routine pre/post checks aren't needed if there are no clinical concerns. ICDs need deactivation. Options 2, 3 and 5 all use monopolar
[Skin surgery: pre-operative checks, anticoagulants & cardiac devices](condition:skin-surgery-preop)
Renal transplant, multiple yellowish facial papules

Ciclosporin is a classic driver. Umbilicated yellow papules with "crown" vessels on dermoscopy. Transplant patients also get many SCCs and BCCs, so examine everything. Fibrofolliculomas suggest Birt-Hogg-Dubé. Syringomas are periorbital. Trichoepitheliomas are skin-coloured and central-facial
[Other skin lumps: neurofibroma, pilomatricoma, myxoid cyst & more](condition:other-skin-lumps)
Gardner syndrome, punctum, malodorous expressible contents

Multiple epidermoid cysts in FAP/Gardner (APC), so check colonoscopy surveillance. A punctum + keratin contents is diagnostic. Dermoid cysts are congenital lines of fusion. Milia are tiny. Hidrocystomas are translucent and periocular
12-year-old boy, hard calcified angulated cheek papule
Children, head and neck, rock-hard, "tent sign", calcification. Pilomatrical carcinoma is rare and occurs in adults. Dermatofibroma is on the legs with a dimple sign
[Other skin lumps: neurofibroma, pilomatricoma, myxoid cyst & more](condition:other-skin-lumps)
68-year-old, multiple painless red papules increasing over years (image), on SGLT2i etc.

Multiple, small, bright red, increasing with age, benign. Reassure. Amelanotic melanoma is usually a *single*, changing, often nodular lesion. HHT gives mucosal/digital telangiectasias with epistaxis. Pyogenic granuloma is solitary and bleeding. No drug causes this
62-year-old street cleaner, firm indurated papillomatous lesion with central crust on the back of the hand for 2 months

Likely cutaneous SCC (or KA, which is treated as SCC): excise with a 4–6 mm margin (BAD cSCC 2020). Curettage alone, PDT and imiquimod are not for invasive SCC. Radiotherapy is for people unfit for surgery
72-year-old woman, gradually enlarging pigmented macule on the side of the face (image)

Irregular, slowly enlarging facial pigmentation in chronically sun-damaged skin. Melanoma in situ, so refer (NG12). Solar lentigo is uniform and stable. SK is stuck-on/waxy. Nodular melanoma is raised
Dorsal distal-phalanx cyst with nail groove, clear jelly
Linked to DIP osteoarthritis. Pressure on the matrix causes a longitudinal groove. Glomus is painful, blue and subungual. Subungual exostosis is hard and under the nail
[Other skin lumps: neurofibroma, pilomatricoma, myxoid cyst & more](condition:other-skin-lumps), [Nail signs: psoriatic nails, Beau’s lines & clubbing](condition:nail-signs)
Lifetime malignant transformation of a single benign intradermal naevus
The per-naevus risk is tiny (estimates ~1 in 200,000/year). Total naevus count matters more than any single mole
70-year-old, 1 year of itchy worsening rash unresponsive to emollients and TCS (image), on ramipril/amlodipine

Persistent "eczema" that fails treatment in older age: exclude **mycosis fungoides/CTCL** (and drug eruption), which needs multiple biopsies. Oral steroids would mask it. Porphyrin screen and PDT are irrelevant
38-year-old woman, longstanding mole, now itchy; dermoscopy image
**Blue naevus** (as the dermoscopy image showed homogeneous steel-blue pigment)
A homogeneous blue structureless pattern is typical. Itch and a family member with melanoma warrant documented review, not alarm
Painful solitary calf nodule for 4 years; eosinophilic tumour, Masson trichrome positive

Masson trichrome stains smooth muscle red. Pilar leiomyomas are painful (cold, touch). Painful skin tumours mnemonic "**ANGEL**" (Angiolipoma, Neuroma, Glomus, Eccrine spiradenoma, Leiomyoma). Of these, only leiomyoma fits the trichrome. Multiple leiomyomas raise the possibility of HLRCC (fumarate hydratase), so consider genetics
20-year-old, previously pigmented mole now changed (white halo)
A symmetrical depigmented rim around a regressing naevus, common in young people (vitiligo link). Refer if the central naevus is atypical or the patient is older
22-year-old, rapidly growing exophytic bleeding hand lesion over 3 weeks
Pyogenic granuloma. C&C removes it and gives tissue for histology. Steroids, antibiotics and reassurance are inappropriate
[Pyogenic granuloma](condition:pyogenic-granuloma), [Skin surgery procedures: excision, curettage, cryotherapy & Mohs](condition:skin-surgery-procedures)
60-year-old runner, firm slightly raised forehead lump of **6 weeks** (image)
BCC vs **keratoacanthoma/SCC**, depending on the image

Six weeks of growth and firmness favour **KA (manage as well-differentiated SCC)**. A pearly rolled edge with telangiectasia would favour BCC. Either way the UK route is **excision and histology**, not watchful waiting. AK is flat/scaly. LM is pigmented
7 mg/kg with adrenaline × 70 = 490 mg = 49 ml of 10 mg/ml. Plain lidocaine max is 3 mg/kg (≈21 ml). Use the BNF/local policy
Warfarin after PE, INR 3.6, cyst excision
**Rebook and ask him to liaise with his anticoagulation team/GP to get INR <3.5**

Don't stop warfarin unilaterally (PE indication). INR 3.6 is above the usual skin-surgery threshold (≤3.5, checked within 72 h). Missing doses or stopping for 3 days without the anticoagulation team risks VTE
[Skin surgery: pre-operative checks, anticoagulants & cardiac devices](condition:skin-surgery-preop)
54-year-old sunbather, enlarging, well-demarcated, red, scaly, crusted plaque on each lower leg

A **well-demarcated** red scaly *plaque* on the lower legs of a woman is classic Bowen's. AK is a rough, ill-defined small macule or papule on the head and hands. UK management: 5-FU, imiquimod, PDT, cryotherapy, or C&C (BAD 2014 guideline)
6-year-old, yellow hairless scalp plaque since birth, thickening
Naevus sebaceous. The commonest secondary tumour is **trichoblastoma**, then syringocystadenoma papilliferum. BCC is rare (old data overestimated it). Excision is elective
% of melanomas arising in a pre-existing naevus
Most melanomas arise de novo, so new or changing lesions matter most
[Melanocytic naevi (moles) & the changing mole](condition:melanocytic-naevi), [Melanoma: recognition & referral](condition:melanoma)
pT1a has a 5-year melanoma-specific survival of ~98–99%
Recurrent pigmentation at a shave-excision scar within 3 months, confined to the scar
Pigment confined to the scar, early recurrence, benign original histology. **Always get the original histology** and refer if it spreads beyond the scar
**Halfway down the *posterior* border of sternocleidomastoid, ~2–3 cm above the clavicle; spinal accessory nerve**, which causes trapezius weakness and shoulder drop (option 2)
The accessory nerve runs superficially in the posterior triangle. The marginal mandibular nerve is at the jaw, not Erb's point. The anterior border options are wrong anatomically

article.title: Where the course answer differs from UK practice

list: **M2 Q3 (BCC diagnosis):** shave biopsy is not ideal for nodular BCC. Use diagnostic excision (4 mm margin) or punch biopsy (BAD BCC guidance).
**M2 Q8 (pacemaker):** UK dermatological surgery teaching says **bipolar**. Routine pre/post checks aren't needed for a stable pacemaker; ICDs differ.
